name.en: “Hi Mam, Hi Dad”: a text from your child on a new number asking for money

how.en: A text or WhatsApp message from an unknown number says it is your son or daughter with a lost or broken phone. Soon they ask for help paying for something urgently, to a bank account they give you. Some ask for your card number, add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay, and then ask you for the code your bank just sent.

text.en: A message from an unknown number says it is your child.
They say their phone is lost or broken and this is a new number.
They ask you to pay something urgently for them.
Some ask for your card number and the code your bank sends you.
Hi Mam it’s me, phone fell in the sink so this is my new number for now 🙈 Are you around? I have a bill I need paid today and can’t get into my banking app, will fix you up at the weekend x

en: hi dad message asking for money
son texted from a new number
daughter broke her phone and needs a bill paid
child asked for my card number and bank code
message from unknown number saying its my kid
A family member writing from a number you don’t have.
An urgent payment to a bank account you don’t know.
Asking for your card number or a code from your bank.
Ring your child on the number you already have before doing anything.
Never share your card details or a bank code by message.
If you paid, call your bank straight away and report it to the Gardaí.

sources.title: Wave of ‘Hi Mam / Hi Dad..’ and bank impersonation scam texts in circulation
